minutes.headline: Select Board conditionally approved a limousine license, took Flat Hill easements by eminent domain, and ratified a new executive assistant.
minutes.summary: The board heard a long public comment period, a regional website funding ask, and a limousine license application for a non-emergency medical transport business, which it approved conditionally on proof of insurance. It voted an order of taking for two easements for the Flat Hill Road bridge project, ratified the executive assistant appointment, approved an ARPA subrecipient grant agreement, and met with the Village at Flat Hill trustees about detention basin maintenance and drainage. The Conrad's hearing was opened and continued to next week, and the town manager reported on budget inputs and the 40S and Chapter 70 explanation.

public_comment.topic: Complained about how the board discussed him on January 9th, texts and emails, private roads at Village at Flat Hill, snow and emergency access, and nepotism concerns.
Alleged a selectman acted in a dual capacity in cemetery commission matters, cited emails and a FOIA request, and argued the cemetery commission lacks authority.
Disputed that the association has been asked to fix the basin for years, questioned the earlier engineering study and capital funds, and called for professional direction.
Asked for a study of where water from a neighboring yard and an empty lot is coming from.
Thanked the trustees for engaging and described ten years of flooding.
Asked for a camera inspection of storm drains at the Flat Hill and Page turn and for pipe sizing and extra drainage.
Asked the board to elevate associate member Kim Duffy to full member of the Green Communities Committee.
Requested appointment as a full member of the Green Communities Committee.

votes.motion: Approve the limousine license for George Carilla d/b/a Metago Transportation LLC at 313 Reservoir Road, conditional on proof of insurance and liability.
Ratify the town manager's appointment of Annie Aubry as executive assistant to the town manager and select board.
Order of taking by eminent domain of temporary and permanent easements at 890 and 914 Flat Hill Road for the bridge project, with damages awarded.
Open the Conrad's hearing and continue it to February 20 at 6:45 p.m.
Accept and approve the ARPA subrecipient grant agreement as printed.

budget_items.what_was_said: Request for the town's share of a regional website, revised down from the agenda amount. Board open but wants a written proposal and estimates.
A member asked how much ARPA remains; the chair gave a rough number.
Awards based on appraisals for the two easement properties.

budget_items.what_was_said: A resident said money remains earmarked in the capital plan for the project and referred to an earlier engineering study bid.

budget_items.what_was_said: A town official noted the per-household cost and total of the work for the association.

budget_items.what_was_said: One proposal from RRC received for three fiscal years and the bid was awarded.
FEMA denied the state's request; the state plans to appeal and appropriated funds that may reimburse towns.
Reimbursement for old expenses will be taken as a local receipt toward the closeout balance.
Final increase for active plans is lower than the earlier estimate and the revised range.
Monty Tech school committee reviewed a budget increase and will vote March 6th.
Contract with BP for 48 months at a rate slightly below the current rate.
Emergency management and firefighter safety grants for rescue suits, saws and radios.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town lost 40S eligibility because the jump in Chapter 70 attributed a high per-pupil amount to out-of-town children; local receipts also factor in.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member remarked on a very large jump in the figure.
Accounts payable, payroll adjustment and payroll warrants were read.

decisions.decision: Board signalled openness to the regional website funding request and asked for a formal written proposal with estimates.
Conrad's hearing to be opened and continued to February 20 at 6:45 p.m.
Village at Flat Hill to seek conservation permission and dredge the basin; town engineer to review scope, do an as-built survey and inspect afterwards; board to send a letter of support.
Engineer committed to look into the camera inspection and a plan for the Flat Hill and Page Street drains.
Kim Duffy's elevation to full Green Communities Committee member goes on next week's agenda without her needing to attend.
February 20 meeting begins at 7:00 with the state delegation and the regular meeting at 8:30; site walk set for Saturday at 10:00.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 4-0 to take temporary and permanent easements at two Flat Hill Road properties by eminent domain for the bridge project, with damages awarded.
The board approved a limousine license for a non-emergency medical transport business, conditional on proof of insurance and liability; the count was not audible.
The board opened the Conrad's hearing and continued it to February 20 at 6:45 p.m.
The board ratified the town manager's executive assistant appointment and approved an ARPA subrecipient grant agreement; the counts were not audible.
Village at Flat Hill trustees will seek conservation permission to dredge a detention basin, and the town engineer will review the scope and look into a drain camera inspection.

why_it_matters: The easement takings are the land step for the Flat Hill Road bridge project, and the damages awarded are a cost the town carries, set from appraisals of the two properties.

The basin and drainage work shows who is responsible for maintaining a private development's stormwater system and when the town's engineer is asked to step in, a question that can come back as a capital or maintenance request.
The town manager's budget inputs (health insurance, electricity, Monty Tech, FEMA storm reimbursement) feed the coming budget and the Proposition 2½ levy picture residents will vote on.
watch_next: February 20: the Conrad's hearing resumes at 6:45 p.m., and the Green Communities Committee appointment for Kim Duffy is on the agenda.
Monty Tech's school committee votes on its budget on March 6, and the regional website funding ask awaits a formal written proposal with estimates.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on every vote that both carry (five votes, all passed 4-0 where our recording gives an outcome) and on most figures. Most differences are caption misrenderings of names and digits. The one thing a reader should know is that our minutes record no outcome for four of the five votes ("not audible"), so the passed 4-0-0 results for those rest on the official minutes alone.
